title: Product overview + PRD: Redwood API, Dedicated & Optimize - Roadmap, Pricing, Release Notes (2026 Q1)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD fragments, design constraints, roadmap and themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Redwood product surface in scope for 2026 Q1

It covers Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Redwood Optimize (cost/performance toolkit). The intent is to provide a single reference for PMs, Eng, Sales, and Support for planning, rollouts, and customer conversations.

1) Product overview

Objective:
- Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Key product surfaces:
- Redwood API (hosted inference): REST/SDK access for text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling, SLA-backed latency/uptime.
- Redwood Optimize: recommendations for batching, quantization, and caching plus cost simulations and quality guardrails.

Primary personas and use cases:
- ML Engineers: optimize throughput/latency and manage rollouts.
- Software Engineers: integrate model calls via SDKs and streaming.
- Platform/Infra: enforce routing, capacity, and cost policies.

2) Goals and success metrics (2026 Q1


Q1

Q1\u2013Q2)

Outcome goals:
- Reduce paid token cost for typical production workloads by 20% (via Optimize recommendations).
- Increase Dedicated conversion (paying reserved customers) from free trial by 12% QoQ.
- Maintain 99.95% regional uptime for Redwood API and 95th percentile latency targets per tier.

Success metrics (target):
- Unit cost reduction: -20% for top-10 customers using Optimize.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for small models; p95 <= 600ms for large-context models on hosted tiers.
- Adoption: 40% of active paid accounts touch Optimize within 90 days.

3) PRD: high-level requirements

Functional requirements:
1. Redwood Optimize UI and API: expose recommended batching/quantization profiles, cost delta estimates, and an Apply workflow that generates a deployment config.
2. Model routing policies: allow customers to configure per-route fallback chains (primary -> cheaper quantized variant -> regional fallback).
3. Pricing calculator: interactive cost model that can run per-customer workload samples and show monthly projection.

Non-functional requirements:
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakouts must be available for any recommended change (Optimize) before and after rollout.
- Safety: recommendations must include a quality delta estimate (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity or cust. eval set) and a rollback threshold.
- Security/compliance: Optimize must never reference PII from customer payloads when surfaced in UI or logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flags exist for Optimize Apply workflow and routing policy editor.
- E2E tests validate cost estimates within +/-10% of measured cost on staging.
- UX: customers can create and run a cost simulation in <= 5 minutes using their own sample traces.

4) Design spec highlights

Architecture:
- Optimize service reads anonymized usage traces from the Observability pipeline (Kafka -> feature extraction -> simulation engine).
- Simulation engine supports per-model/run quantization profiles (FP16, 4-bit, dynamic quant).
- Apply workflow emits a DeploymentSpec YAML that can be consumed by the orchestration layer to instantiate a canary.

Key components (owners):
- Optimize backend (owner: Applied ML) \u2014 cost model, simulation engine, quant profiles.
- Optimize UI (owner: Eng DX) \u2014 interactive simulation, apply flow, results.
- Policy engine (owner: Eng Platform) \u2014 per-route routing/fallback and A/B rollout.

Data & API contracts (examples):
- /v1/optimize/simulate POST {trace_id, model_id, quant_profile} -> {cost_estimate_usd, latency_estimate_ms, quality_score_delta}
- Apply YAML: deployment: {model_id, quant_profile, canary_percent, rollout_schedule, rollback_threshold}

Operational constraints:
- Batch/simulate jobs should complete within 10m for traces <= 10k tokens.
- Canary windows default: 1 hour at 5% traffic, then 3h at 25%, then full if no regressions.

5) Roadmap & themes (Q1
\u2013Q2 2026)

Themes by quarter:
- Q1 2026 (stabilize): Launch Optimize v2 (simulation + Apply), routing policy editor (alpha), pricing calculator MVP.
- Q2 2026 (scale): Scale Optimize recommendations to top-50 customers, Dedicated conversion playbook, extended quant profiles for large-context models.

Milestones and owners:
- 2026-01-15: Optimize v2 backend MVP (Applied ML) \u2014 complete
- 2026-02-01: Optimize UI first-pass (Eng DX) \u2014 complete
- 2026-02-10: Internal beta + controlled canaries for 5 pilot customers (Customer Success) \u2014 in progress
- 2026-03-15: Public release of Optimize Apply + pricing calculator (Product)
- 2026-05-01: Dedicated conversion toolkit + sales playbook (Go-to-market)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization. Mitigation: require customer-provided eval set and automated guardrails; block Apply when quality delta > configurable threshold.
- Risk: Cost estimates diverge from real usage. Mitigation: tie estimates to recent 7/30-day rolling averages and provide uncertainty bands.

6) Pricing & packaging notes

High-level pricing model (guidance for GTM):
- Hosted (Redwood API): usage-based pricing (tokens) with three tiers (Developer, Business, Enterprise). Developer includes free credits.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity pricing (committed $/month per GPU pool + per-token compute overages for bursts). Discounts for 12/24-month commitments.
- Private: platform license fee + per-node support + optional managed updates.
- Optimize: included for Business/Enterprise tiers with limited credits; paid add-on for Developer and Dedicated customers with per-simulation credits or seat-based subscription.

Example price bands (internal guidance):
- Developer: $0.0008 / input token, $0.0015 / output token (introductory rate)
- Business: negotiated, baseline 30% discount vs Developer depending on volume
- Dedicated reserved: $X,XXX per GPU pool/month (example: 4xA100-equivalent pool $12,000/mo) + burst at hosted rates
- Optimize simulation credits: $0.03 per 1,000 simulated tokens (for large traces) or monthly plan $299/mo for 50k tokens simulated.

Bundling & promotions:
- 90-day trial for Dedicated (trial credits + one round of Optimize simulation included).
- Conversion credits: first 3 months discounted for customers who adopt Recommend + Apply in first 60 days.

7) Release notes (v2026.02 \u2014 public release target 2026-03-15)

Highlights:
- Optimize v2: simulation engine with quantization-aware cost/quality estimates and Apply -> DeploymentSpec exports.
- Pricing calculator: interactive per-workload projection in Console.
- Routing policy editor (beta): per-route fallback chains and automatic regional fallback.

User-visible changes:
- New Console section: Optimize -> Simulations.
- API endpoints: /v1/optimize/simulate and /v1/optimize/apply (Apply behind feature flag).
- New telemetry: simulation_id attached to rollout traces for pre/post comparison.

Notable bug fixes & internal improvements:
- Reduced p95 latency variance by 8% for medium models via scheduler improvements (serving-runtime).
- Observability pipeline: token-level cost attribution available down to route+model.

8) Rollout plan & runbook (summary)

Rollout stages:
1. Internal dogfood (2 weeks) \u2014 Product, Eng, CS use Optimize on internal workloads. Owner: Product.
2. Pilot (5 customers) \u2014 Controlled canaries at 1\u20135% traffic. Owner: Customer Success.
3. Early access (20 customers) \u2014 Opt-in via console toggle; 10% traffic canaries. Owner: Sales/CS.
4. Public release \u2014 Feature flag removal for applicable tiers. Owner: Product/Platform.

Rollback triggers:
- Quality delta exceeds configured threshold (default -2% semantic similarity).
- Error rate increase > 2x baseline for the route.
- Latency p95 regression > 50% of baseline.

Contacts & owners:

9) Metrics to monitor post-release

- Adoption: number of customers running >=1 simulation per month; number using Apply.
- Cost impact: median and 90th percentile percent change in $/1k tokens post-Apply.
- Quality regressions: percent of canaries that triggered automatic rollback.
- Performance: p95 latency delta pre/post Apply.
